app.title: Addon Pack Editor - Tudur's Vehicle Mod
app.about:
Addon Pack Editor {version}
An addon pack authoring tool for Tudur's Vehicle Mod
pack.none:
No addon pack is open.
Create or open one from the File menu.
pack.name: Pack name (folder)
pack.hint: The location is normally the tudursvehiclemod-addons folder in your game directory. A namespace may only contain lowercase letters, digits and _ . - (use one unique to your addon).
pack.bad_namespace: A namespace may only contain lowercase letters, digits and _ . -
pack.bad_name: The pack name contains characters that can't be used in a folder name.
pack.exists_open: {path} already exists. Open that folder instead?
pack.not_a_pack: {path} doesn't look like an addon pack (it needs a namespace folder under data/ or assets/).
pack.open_first: Create or open an addon pack first.
vehicles.title: Vehicles
vehicles.name: Vehicle name
vehicles.confirm_delete: Delete the JSON file of vehicle "{name}"? This can't be undone.
vehicle.placeholder: Pick a vehicle on the left, or create one with "New vehicle".
vehicle.fix_json_first: The JSON has a syntax error, so the entity type can't be changed. Fix the error first.
vehicle.cannot_switch:
The JSON has a syntax error, so the form can't be shown.

{err}
vehicle.hidden_kept:
These fields aren't used by this entity type, so the form doesn't show them. Their values are kept and saved unchanged (remove them in manual JSON editing if not needed):

{keys}
vehicle.unknown_type: The tool doesn't know this entity type (if it comes from an addon mod, adding its plugin makes its fields appear).
vehicle.unsaved: Vehicle "{name}" has unsaved changes. Save them?
form.pick_file_tip: Pick a file, copy it into the pack and set its reference
parts.title: OBJ parts
parts.no_model: Set model to an OBJ file inside this pack to list its parts here.
parts.tip: Double-click to copy a part name (typed into the focused field if there is one)
json.not_object: The top level must be an object ({ ... })
json.unknown_key: Unknown field (the mod ignores it). Check the spelling.
json.not_for_type: This entity type doesn't use this field
assets.reference_tip: The string to use when a vehicle JSON (etc.) points at this file
assets.note: Below each fixed location (data/<namespace>/vehicles, assets/<namespace>/models, ...) you can create any subfolders. Weapons, HUD scripts, sounds and HUD textures are referenced by file name alone, so the same file name can't be reused even in different subfolders.
assets.new_folder_prompt: Folder to create (use / for nested folders):
assets.bad_folder: "{part}" can't be used. Only lowercase letters, digits and _ . - are allowed.
assets.folder_not_empty: Only empty folders can be deleted.
assets.bad_type: {name} can't be imported as this kind of file.
assets.subfolder_prompt: Destination folder under {root} (use / for nested folders, leave empty for the top):
assets.name_unique_note: This kind is referenced by file name alone - keep file names unique within the pack.
plugins.load_failed: Some plugins could not be loaded (the tool itself still works).
json.msg.comma: A comma ( , ) is expected. Check for a missing comma at the end of the previous line.
json.msg.colon: A colon ( : ) is expected between a field name and its value.
json.msg.property: Field names must be in double quotes ( " ). Also check for a trailing comma before a closing bracket.
json.msg.value: A value is expected (a missing value, or an extra comma).
json.msg.extra: Unexpected content after the end of the JSON.
json.msg.control: A string contains a character that isn't allowed (a raw newline or tab).
json.legacy_key: Old form (still read for compatibility). Writing it inside "{parent}" is recommended.
weapon.placeholder: Pick a weapon file on the left, or create one with "New weapon".
weapon.name: Weapon name (file name)
weapon.name_hint: e.g. guns/m2_browning (/ for subfolders). A vehicle's weapon_name uses only the file-name part.
weapon.exists: A weapon file named "{name}" already exists (weapons are referenced by file name alone, so the name can't be reused even in another folder).
weapon.custom_type: A custom weapon type added by an addon mod.
weapon.no_equals: This line has no "=" - the mod ignores it.
weapon.unknown_key: This mod doesn't read this key (MC Heli-only, or a typo). It is ignored.
weapon.duplicate: The same key appears again on line {line}. The mod uses the later one, so this line has no effect.
weapon.not_number: Not a number - the default value is used instead.
weapon.truncated: An integer field - the fractional part is dropped.
weapon.bad_choice: Unrecognized value - the default is used (choices: {choices}).
weapon.extra_columns: Too many values - only the first {n} are used.
weapon.col_default_used: The default is used for this column.
weapon.wp_int: {col} must be a whole number ("{v}") - decimals aren't accepted.
weapon.wp_speed_clamped: speed% ({v}) is outside 0-100; the mod clamps it to a safe range.
weapon.item_name: Material "{v}" isn't allowed (iron_ingot / gunpowder / redstone only).
weapon.no_type: No Type - this weapon can't fire (treated as OTHER).
weapon.bad_type: Type "{v}" isn't recognized - treated as OTHER, which never fires.
weapon.cas_needs_aircraft: CAS needs CasAircraft; without it, firing does nothing.
weapon.cas_needs_waypoint: CAS needs at least one valid CasWaypoint; without it, firing does nothing.
weapon.carrier_needs_waypoint: Carrier needs at least one valid CarrierWaypoint; without it the launch is disabled.
weapon.carrier_needs_landing: Carrier needs at least one valid CarrierLandingWaypoint; without it the launch is disabled.
hud.name: HUD name (file name)
hud.name_hint: e.g. aircraft/jet (/ for subfolders). A vehicle's hud uses only the file-name part. New files start with the default template.
hud.exists: A HUD script named "{name}" already exists (HUD scripts are referenced by file name alone).
hud.placeholder: Pick a HUD script on the left, or create one with "New HUD".
hud.replace_confirm: Replace the current content with the template?
hud.preview_tip: Preview drawn with the sample values. Click an element to jump to its line. Red dashed boxes mark elements outside the screen.
hud.all_on_tip: Turns on every state (reloading, stall, low fuel, ...) to check for overlaps and off-screen elements.
hud.unknown_directive: "{d}" is not a known directive; the mod skips this line.
hud.too_few_args: {d} needs at least {n} arguments (found {got}); the mod skips this line.
hud.color_args: Color takes 1 argument (packed ARGB) or 4 (a, r, g, b); anything else is ignored and the color stays unchanged.
hud.line_too_short: A line needs at least 2 points (4 numbers); nothing is drawn.
hud.line_odd: Odd number of coordinates; the last one is unused.
hud.stray_endif: EndIf without a matching If; the line is ignored (possibly caused by a nested If).
hud.nested_if: An If inside an If isn't supported: this If is ignored and the next EndIf closes the OUTER If.
hud.unclosed_if: Missing EndIf: everything to the end of the file becomes part of this If.
hud.radar_unsupported: Radars aren't implemented in this mod; nothing is drawn.
hud.unknown_var: There is no variable "{v}"; the mod silently uses 0 (check the spelling).
hud.string_var_numeric: "{v}" is a string variable; outside DrawString's %s it evaluates to 0.
hud.fixed_var: "{v}" exists only for compatibility; its value is always fixed (not implemented).
hud.call_missing: Called script "{name}" isn't in this pack; the mod does nothing (fine if another pack provides it).
hud.texture_missing: Texture "{name}" isn't in textures/gui of this pack (fine if another pack provides it).
hud.offscreen: Drawn outside a {w}×{h} screen (with the current sample values).
hud.offscreen_called: Something drawn by called script "{name}" falls outside a {w}×{h} screen.
hud.err_empty: Empty expression (a missing argument or an extra comma): {expr}
